ordered_diagnoses: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) with acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (ACLE)

candidates.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE) with acute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (ACLE)
support_spans: A 22-year-old woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus
Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face, nose, ears, and medial forehead
candidates.why: The patient's history of SLE and presentation of erythematous plaques in the malar distribution support this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS)
support_spans: Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm
candidates.why: The presence of target lesions and blisters on the skin, particularly on the palms and soles, is consistent with SJS.

candidates.name: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN)
support_spans: Flaccid bullae and target lesions
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes
candidates.why: The presence of bullae, target lesions, and full-thickness epithelial necrosis on biopsy supports the diagnosis of TEN.

key_evidence_spans: A 22-year-old woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus
Erythematous plaques with superficial desquamation in the malar distribution of the face, nose, ears, and medial forehead
Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles

candidates.name: Rowell syndrome
support_spans: Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Positive anti-Smith, antiribonucleoprotein, and SSA/anti-Ro antibodies
candidates.why: The combination of lupus erythematosus and atypical target lesions with positive anti-Smith, antiribonucleoprotein, and SSA/anti-Ro antibodies is suggestive of Rowell syndrome.
candidates.protected_reason: Rowell syndrome is a rare condition that may be overlooked in favor of more common diagnoses, such as systemic lupus erythematosus or erythema multiforme.

candidates.name: Erythema multiforme
support_spans: Numerous flat and raised 2-zoned atypical targets with dusky centers on the forearms, abdomen, back, thighs, legs, palms and soles
Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm
candidates.why: The presence of target lesions and blisters is consistent with erythema multiforme, which can be triggered by various factors, including infections and medications.
candidates.protected_reason: Erythema multiforme is a distinct entity that may be underdiagnosed in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, and its recognition is important for appropriate management.

candidates.name: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
support_spans: Worsening, exquisitely tender rash with several blisters across right arm
Punch biopsy of abdominal target lesion showed dyskeratosis with superficial perivascular inflammation and interface changes
contradict_spans: Negative bacterial blood, urine, stool and cerebrospinal fluid cultures
candidates.why: The presence of blisters, erosions, and interface changes on biopsy is consistent with toxic epidermal necrolysis, which can be triggered by medications or infections.
candidates.protected_reason: Toxic epidermal necrolysis is a life-threatening condition that requires prompt recognition and treatment, and its diagnosis may be challenging in patients with underlying systemic lupus erythematosus.
